name: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Type 9
aliases: Combined Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation Deficiency Type 9

criteria.description: Presence of multisystem clinical manifestations consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction including neurological and muscular symptoms
Demonstration of combined defects in multiple respiratory chain enzyme complexes in muscle or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic variants in nuclear genes affecting oxidative phosphorylation complexes
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers or cytochrome c oxidase (COX)-deficient fibers

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multisystem clinical features plus biochemical evidence of combined respiratory chain defects and genetic confirmation of pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to phenotypic heterogeneity.

pathognomonic.notes: Elevated blood lactate due to mitochondrial dysfunction

common.notes: Reduced muscle tone commonly observed in infancy
Delayed acquisition of motor and cognitive milestones
Various seizure types including generalized and focal
Dilated or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy may develop

occasional.notes: Poor growth in infancy and early childhood

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
Combined deficiency of respiratory chain complexes I, III, and IV enzyme activities in muscle biopsy
Elevated serum creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia and brainstem signal abnormalities
Muscle MRI demonstrating fatty infiltration and atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial respiratory chain complex subunits or assembly factors
Mitochondrial DNA depletion or multiple deletions may be present
other: Muscle biopsy revealing ragged-red fibers and COX-negative fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Stroke-like episodes with focal neurological deficits
Characteristic brain MRI findings with stroke-like lesions
Subacute painless vision loss in young adults
Primary involvement of optic nerve without multisystem disease

redFlags: Rapidly progressive external ophthalmoplegia in infancy or early childhood
Severe lactic acidosis refractory to treatment
Multisystem involvement including cardiomyopathy and neurological deterioration
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
